label: <DEL> step after originals containing 1/z/l/s/a/n/p/q/b/k
explanation: Mostly a delimiter-step unit: 76% of activation mass is at the <DEL> step (39% of <DEL> steps fire, 7.9x lift). Whether and how strongly it fires at <DEL> depends on which tokens appeared in the original sequence. Tokens 1, z, l, s, a, n, p, q, b, k raise it, especially as the first token (first_tok 1/z/l/s/a has about 2x lift). Requiring at least 2 of these tokens among the originals raises precision from 0.39 to 0.55, and requiring 3 raises it to 0.69 at lower recall, so the drive looks graded and roughly additive over the prefix. The predicate is an approximation of that. Longer sequences fire more often. The remaining mass is weaker: about 18% comes from late original-phase steps (rate rises with t; inputs e/t/u most often, mostly first occurrences of a token), and about 6.5% from the first one or two copy steps. It never fires at t=0 or 1 and almost never deep in the copy phase (recall_idx >= 4).
